specName: Semantic Wiring — Connect pgvector + AGE to Spec Generation & Execution
title: rorca-semantic-wiring
_notes: The pgvector embeddings table, hybrid search (keyword + semantic RRF), Apache AGE knowledge graph, graph-context traversal, and memory-router (CAG/RAG) are all BUILT but NOT WIRED into spec generation or execution. This spec connects them: embeddings get populated, spec generation queries vector search + graph context, execution engine injects graph-derived memories/conventions per story, and the UI shows semantic retrieval stats in context injection cards.
_relatesTo: rorca-postgres-migration (built the infrastructure, PG-007 through PG-019). rorca-context-intent-engine (CIE-004 context routing, already wired). Independent — can run immediately.
_executionOrder: Run immediately. All infrastructure exists. No new tables or extensions needed. Only migration is 057 (spec_search_index tsvector trigger for auto-indexing on spec insert/update).

userStories.title: Populate Embeddings on Spec Approval + Run Completion
userStories.description:
The embedding pipeline (`backend/src/lib/embedding-pipeline.ts`) is started on server boot (`server.ts:277`) and subscribes to WAL events, but the `embedText()` function requires an API key (OPENAI_API_KEY or VOYAGE_API_KEY) which most self-hosted users won't have. Add a FREE local embedding fallback using the existing `pg_trgm` extension for trigram similarity when no embedding API key is available.

1. In `embedding-pipeline.ts`, add a `localEmbedding()` function that generates a sparse TF-IDF vector (1536 dimensions, zero-padded) from the input text using term frequencies. This is NOT as good as OpenAI embeddings but enables vector search without an API key. Use `prepareText()` (already exists at line ~180) to clean input before vectorizing.
2. Modify `resolveApiKey()` (line ~85) to return a sentinel `'local'` value instead of throwing when no API key is found. Update `embedText()` to check for this sentinel and call `localEmbedding()` instead of the HTTP providers.
3. Verify that `startEmbeddingPipeline()` (line ~600) correctly handles `spec_approved`, `run_finished`, and `memory_created` WAL events by checking the WAL subscription filter in `sse-hub.ts`. Currently it subscribes but the handler may silently fail if the workspace_id resolution fails — add a `try/catch` with `logger.warn` around each handler.
4. Add `logger.info` statements showing embedding queue depth after each enqueue batch (e.g., `[embedding] Queued 5 stories from spec rorca-semantic-wiring (queue depth: 12)`).
acceptanceCriteria: When no OPENAI_API_KEY or VOYAGE_API_KEY is set, embeddings are still generated using local TF-IDF vectorization
localEmbedding() produces a 1536-dimension float array from term frequencies
resolveApiKey() returns 'local' sentinel instead of throwing when no API keys found
embedText() dispatches to localEmbedding() when provider is 'local'
WAL event handlers (spec_approved, run_finished, memory_created) have try/catch with logger.warn
Logger shows queue depth after each enqueue batch
Approving a spec in the UI triggers embedding generation for all stories within 5 seconds
Running a pipeline triggers re-embedding of completed stories (with outcome status) within 5 seconds

userStories.title: Auto-Index Specs in tsvector for Keyword Search
userStories.description:
The `spec_search_index` table (migration 044) exists for full-text keyword search but is NOT auto-populated when specs are created or approved. Create migration `057_spec_search_auto_index.sql` that adds a trigger to auto-populate `spec_search_index` when rows are inserted/updated in `spec_versions`.

1. Create `backend/src/db/pg-migrations/057_spec_search_auto_index.sql`:
   - Add a function `update_spec_search_index()` that extracts `title`, `userStories[*].title`, `userStories[*].description`, and `userStories[*].acceptanceCriteria` from the `content` jsonb column of `spec_versions`, concatenates them, and upserts into `spec_search_index` with `to_tsvector('english', concatenated_text)`.
   - Create trigger `trg_spec_versions_search` on `spec_versions` AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE that calls `update_spec_search_index()`.
2. In `backend/src/routes/specs.ts`, after the `INSERT INTO spec_versions` call (around line 920 where spec is saved after generation), verify the trigger fires automatically. No manual insert into `spec_search_index` needed.
3. Backfill: in the migration, run a one-time `INSERT INTO spec_search_index ... SELECT FROM spec_versions` to index all existing specs.

Trigger update_spec_search_index() fires on spec_versions INSERT/UPDATE

userStories.title: Wire retrieveContext() into Spec Generation Prompt
userStories.description:
The spec generation endpoint (`POST /api/specs/generate` in `backend/src/routes/specs.ts` around line 700-900) currently uses `synthesizeWithMeta()` (plaintext direction stack) + `buildCatalogContext()` (filesystem skills/memory/agents). It does NOT use `retrieveContext()` from `memory-router.ts` which provides CAG/RAG tiered retrieval with vector search fallback.

Replace the manual context assembly with `retrieveContext()` to add semantic search:

1. Import `retrieveContext` from `../lib/memory-router` at the top of specs.ts.
2. After the existing `synthesizeWithMeta()` call (line ~717), call `retrieveContext(workspaceId, brief, { maxTokens: 16000, includeGraph: true })` where `brief` is the user's spec brief text.
3. The `retrieveContext()` result includes `memory` (scored entries), `skills` (matched by relevance), `graphContext` (related memories/conventions from AGE), and `meta` (cagHits, ragHits, graphHits, latencyMs).
4. Append the `graphContext.graphSection` (formatted markdown from `formatGraphContext()`) to the LLM prompt AFTER the direction stack section and BEFORE the skill catalog. This injects related memories, conventions, and file history from the knowledge graph.
5. Update `precomputedContextSummary` (line ~769) to include new fields: `vectorHits: meta.ragHits`, `graphHits: meta.graphHits`, `retrievalTier: meta.tier`, `retrievalLatencyMs: meta.latencyMs`.
6. Keep `buildCatalogContext()` for skills/personas — `retrieveContext()` supplements it with vector-retrieved memories, it does NOT replace the filesystem catalog.
7. Do NOT remove the existing `synthesizeWithMeta()` call — `retrieveContext()` enhances the direction stack, it doesn't replace it.
acceptanceCriteria: retrieveContext() is called during spec generation with the brief as storyText
includeGraph is set to true so AGE knowledge graph is queried
graphSection from retrieveContext() is appended to the LLM prompt after direction stack
precomputedContextSummary includes vectorHits, graphHits, retrievalTier, retrievalLatencyMs
If retrieveContext() throws (graph unavailable, no embeddings), spec generation still succeeds using existing plaintext context
Existing synthesizeWithMeta() and buildCatalogContext() calls are preserved
The context injection summary card in the UI shows the new fields (vectorHits, graphHits)
npx tsc --noEmit passes in backend/

userStories.title: Wire Graph Context into Execution Engine buildPrompt()
userStories.description:
The execution engine (`backend/src/lib/execution-engine.ts`) runs each story as a subprocess. `buildPrompt()` (line ~467) assembles the prompt from story metadata, context files, personas, and skills — but does NOT query the knowledge graph for related memories, conventions, or file history.

Add graph context injection to `buildPrompt()`:

1. Change `buildPrompt()` signature to accept an optional `graphSection?: string` parameter (after `skillsSection`).
2. In the prompt assembly (both `impl` and `qa` modes), insert `graphSection` AFTER the skills section and BEFORE the workflow instructions. Wrap it in a clear delimiter: `\n=== RELATED HISTORY (from knowledge graph) ===\n{graphSection}\n=== END RELATED HISTORY ===\n`.
3. In the caller of `buildPrompt()` (around line ~2030 where `const prompt = buildPrompt(...)` is called), add a graph context fetch BEFORE the buildPrompt call:
   - Import `getGraphContext` and `formatGraphContext` from `./graph-context`.
   - Extract predicted file paths from the story using a new `extractPredictedPaths(story)` helper that regex-matches file paths (patterns like `src/`, `backend/`, `.tsx`, `.ts`, `.sql`, `.md`) from the story's description + acceptance criteria.
   - Call `const graphCtx = await getGraphContext(story.id, predictedPaths, workspaceId)` wrapped in try/catch (graph is optional).
   - Call `const graphSection = graphCtx ? formatGraphContext(graphCtx) : ''`.
   - Pass `graphSection` to `buildPrompt()`.
4. Add the `extractPredictedPaths()` helper function near `buildPrompt()`. It should use a regex like `/(?:src|backend|frontend|lib|components|routes|hooks|panels|db|migrations)/[\w\-\/\.]+\.[a-z]+/g` to extract plausible file paths from story text.
acceptanceCriteria: buildPrompt() accepts optional graphSection parameter
Graph section is injected between skills section and workflow instructions in both impl and qa modes
extractPredictedPaths() extracts file paths from story description + acceptance criteria
getGraphContext() is called with story.id and predicted paths before buildPrompt()
If getGraphContext() throws or returns empty, buildPrompt() proceeds without graph context
Graph context includes related memories, conventions, and file history when available
The === RELATED HISTORY === delimiter is used for clear separation

userStories.title: Populate Knowledge Graph After Each Story Completion
userStories.description:
The graph populator (`backend/src/lib/graph-populator.ts`, 106 lines) subscribes to WAL events and calls `populateFromRun()` / `populateFromSpec()` — but it only handles `run_finished` and `spec_approved` events. It does NOT create file-touch edges from `story_commits` during a run (only after the entire run finishes).

Enhance the graph populator for continuous per-story population:

1. In `graph-populator.ts`, add a handler for the `story_passed` WAL event type. When a story passes:
   - Call `addStoryNode()` with the story metadata (id, specId, title, status='pass').
   - Query `story_commits` for this story's committed files: `SELECT file_path FROM story_commits WHERE run_id = $1 AND story_id = $2`.
   - For each file path, call `addFileTouch(storyId, filePath, workspaceId)`.
   - If the story had matched skills (check `story_results.matched_skills` jsonb column), call `addSkillUsage(skillName, storyId, 'auto-match')` for each.
2. Add a handler for `story_failed` events — same as above but with status='fail'.
3. Add a handler for `memory_created` events — call `addMemoryLink(memoryId, sourceStoryId, category)` to create Memory-LEARNED_FROM->Story edges.
4. Ensure `isGraphAvailable()` is checked at the top of each handler — if AGE is not installed, return early (graceful degradation per PG-019).
acceptanceCriteria: story_passed WAL events trigger graph population with story node + file-touch edges
story_failed WAL events trigger graph population with failed status
memory_created WAL events create Memory-LEARNED_FROM->Story edges
story_commits are queried for file paths on each story completion
Matched skills create Skill-USED_IN->Story edges
isGraphAvailable() is checked before any graph operation
If AGE is unavailable, handlers return early with no errors
Logger shows node/edge creation counts per story

userStories.title: Update Context Injection Summary UI with Semantic Stats
userStories.description:
The context injection summary card (`src/components/ContextSummaryCard.tsx` or equivalent in `src/panels/SpecForgePanelPage.tsx`) shows direction layers, skills, memory entries, schema, and git memory with checkmarks/crosses. It does NOT show vector search hits, graph context hits, or retrieval tier.

Update the UI to display semantic retrieval stats:

1. Find the `ContextSummary` TypeScript interface (likely in `src/panels/SpecForgeOutput.tsx` or `src/panels/SpecForgePanelPage.tsx`) and add: `vectorHits?: number`, `graphHits?: number`, `retrievalTier?: 'cache' | 'search' | 'hybrid'`, `retrievalLatencyMs?: number`.
2. In the context summary card rendering, add a new row after the existing rows:
   - **Vector Search**: Show `✅ {vectorHits} hits` if vectorHits > 0, otherwise `⬚ No embeddings` (grey, not red — embeddings are optional).
   - **Knowledge Graph**: Show `✅ {graphHits} nodes` if graphHits > 0, otherwise `⬚ No graph data` (grey).
   - **Retrieval Mode**: Show a small badge like `cache`, `search`, or `hybrid` next to the vector row.
3. Use `text-zinc-400` for the "not available" states (NOT red — these are optional features, not errors).
4. Add a tooltip on hover explaining: "Vector search and knowledge graph require embeddings. Run POST /api/admin/embed-all or set OPENAI_API_KEY to enable."

userStories.title: Backfill Existing Specs and Memories into Embeddings Table
userStories.description:
The backfill endpoint `POST /api/admin/embed-all` exists in `backend/src/routes/backups.ts` (line ~117) and calls `backfillAll()` from `embedding-pipeline.ts`. However:

1. `backfillAll()` (line ~520 in embedding-pipeline.ts) queries `spec_versions` for specs and `memories` for memory entries, but it may miss specs that don't have `spec_versions` rows (older specs stored only as JSON files on disk).
2. Add a filesystem fallback to `backfillAll()`: after querying `spec_versions`, also scan `forge/specs/approved/*.json` and `forge/specs/pending/*.json` from ALL registered workspaces (query `workspaces` table for paths). For each spec JSON found on disk but NOT in `spec_versions`, read the file, extract story text, and enqueue embedding jobs.
3. Add a `GET /api/admin/embed-all/status` enhancement: include `embeddingCount` (total rows in `embeddings` table), `specCount` (distinct source_type='spec'), `storyCount` (distinct source_type='story'), `memoryCount` (distinct source_type='memory') in the response alongside existing queue stats.
4. After backfill completes, log a summary: `[embedding] Backfill complete: {queued} jobs queued, {skippedStale} skipped (unchanged)`.
acceptanceCriteria: backfillAll() scans filesystem spec JSONs from all registered workspaces as fallback
Specs on disk but not in spec_versions are included in backfill

Backfill completion logs a summary with queued and skipped counts
Running POST /api/admin/embed-all populates the embeddings table with all existing specs/stories/memories
Staleness check (content_hash) prevents re-embedding unchanged content

userStories.title: Populate Convention Graph Edges from .rorca/config.json Scopes
userStories.description:
The knowledge graph has Convention nodes and APPLIES_TO edges (`backend/src/lib/knowledge-graph.ts`), but they're never populated. Convention rules live in `.rorca/config.json` under `routing.scopes` (path globs with injected context files) and `routing.tags` (tag-based injection).

Add convention population from config:

1. Create a new function `populateConventionsFromConfig(workspaceId: string, workspacePath: string)` in `knowledge-graph.ts` (or a new `convention-graph.ts` file).
2. Load `.rorca/config.json` via `loadRorcaConfig(workspacePath)` (from `rorca-config.ts`).
3. For each `routing.scopes` entry: create a Convention node with `name = inject[0]` (the context file), `source = 'config.json'`, `layer = 'scope'`. Create an APPLIES_TO edge from Convention to each matched file (use `micromatch` against a file listing from `fs.readdirSync` or the workspace directory tree).
4. For each `routing.globals` entry: create a Convention node with `name = global_file`, `source = 'config.json'`, `layer = 'global'`.
5. Call `populateConventionsFromConfig()` from the graph populator when it processes `spec_approved` events (conventions should be in the graph before stories reference them).
6. Also call it from `POST /api/workspaces/:id/rorca-config` (the config save endpoint in `backend/src/routes/workspaces.ts`) so convention graph stays in sync when users edit config.
acceptanceCriteria: populateConventionsFromConfig() creates Convention nodes from routing.scopes and routing.globals
Convention-APPLIES_TO->File edges are created using micromatch against workspace files
Convention nodes have name, source ('config.json'), and layer ('scope' or 'global') properties
Called during spec_approved graph population
Called when config is saved via PUT /api/workspaces/:id/rorca-config
isGraphAvailable() checked before any graph operations

2. Add these fields to the `context_summary` jsonb that gets inserted into `spec_generation_logs` (around line ~920 where the log INSERT happens):

userStories.title: Add Embedding Dimension Flexibility for Local vs API Providers
userStories.description:
The `embeddings` table has a fixed `vector(1536)` column (matching OpenAI text-embedding-3-small). The local TF-IDF fallback (SW-001) also produces 1536 dimensions. But if a user switches from local to OpenAI or vice versa, existing embeddings become incompatible (cosine similarity between TF-IDF and neural embeddings is meaningless).

Add provider tracking and automatic re-embedding on provider change:

1. The `embeddings.model` column already exists (TEXT). Ensure `localEmbedding()` (from SW-001) writes `model = 'local-tfidf'` and API embeddings write `model = 'text-embedding-3-small'` (or whichever API model is used).
2. In `hybridSearch()` (`backend/src/lib/search.ts`), add a check: if the query embedding was generated with a different model than the stored embeddings, log a warning: `[search] Mixed embedding models detected (query: {queryModel}, stored: {storedModel}). Results may be degraded. Run POST /api/admin/embed-all to re-embed with current provider.`
3. In `backfillAll()`, add an optional `force?: boolean` parameter. When `force=true`, skip the content_hash staleness check and re-embed everything (used when switching providers). Expose this via `POST /api/admin/embed-all` body: `{ force: true }`.
4. Add a `GET /api/admin/embedding-provider` endpoint that returns `{ provider: 'openai' | 'voyage' | 'local', model: string, dimensions: number }`.
acceptanceCriteria: Local TF-IDF embeddings are stored with model='local-tfidf'
API embeddings are stored with their actual model name
hybridSearch() logs a warning when query and stored embedding models differ
backfillAll() accepts force parameter to skip staleness check
POST /api/admin/embed-all accepts { force: true } in request body
GET /api/admin/embedding-provider returns current provider, model, and dimensions
